newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq ready to talk with U.S. - paper.
newsitem.headline: Iraq ready to talk with U.S. - paper.

text.p: The ruling Baath party newspaper al-Thawra said on Thursday Baghdad was prepared to open a dialogue with the United States.
"Iraq realises quite well that the United States is a superpower with vital interests in the region. Iraq does not want to threaten these interests," declared Thawra in a front- page editorial.
"Iraq has no interest in fighting the United States or being hostile to it. It has more than one advantage in dealing with it," the paper added.
The paper said isolating or containing Iraq would not serve U.S. interests in the region.
Washington leads a tough anti-Iraq camp at the U.N. Security Council.
Iraq's President Saddam Hussein in remarks published on Wednesday called the United States the worst despot history had ever known.
Thawra warned that Washington's "blind enmity" towards the government in Baghdad would eventually destroy its interests in the region.
"If Iraq is not allowed to have a normal international way of life, enjoying security and stability, the region's security will remain under threat, without stability," Thawra said.
Thawra urged Washington to give up attempts to topple the Iraqi government. It said the 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait and the U.N. trade embargo had failed to change the regime.
"The current (U.S.) administration, like its predecessor, has drastically failed in achieving its aims in the forefront of them the removal of the ruling regime in Iraq," it said.
Thawra said a dialogue with Iraq and the lifting of sanctions were the prerequisites for peace and stability in the area.
